newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Havel appeals for quick end to Czech rail strike.
newsitem.headline: Havel appeals for quick end to Czech rail strike.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel on Thursday appealed to unions to end the country's rail strike and asked ministers to quickly draw up plans to revitalise the entire rail transport system.

"The President...appeals to unions to call off the strike as soon as possible and asks the government to speed up preparations of a complex and concrete conception to reform the whole public transport system," a presidential statement said.
The strike was extended to a third day on Thursday as both unions and the government dug in their heels, adopting hardline stances.

Unions, which called the strike on Sunday, are demanding the removal of Czech Railway's management and a total rethink of plans to reform the dilapidated rail system which could cost tens of thousands of jobs.
However, Prime Minster Vaclav Klaus who espouses Thatcherite free-market policies while often showing a willingness to compromise in practice, has taken a tough line against the strikers.
Earlier on Thursday he called their methods "irresponsible" and their demands "unacceptable" saying he would not meet union leaders until the strike was called off.
"I would like to stress that the way this strike was started, the way it is being led, and the demands which are being made, (my party) considers completely unacceptable," Klaus said.

Rail unions began a 48-hour strike at the stroke of midnight on Tuesday, but extended it for another day on Wednesday evening. They have threatened to prolong the stoppage further if an acceptable compromise is not reached.
The strike is the first major confrontation between organised labour and the government since the fall of communism in 1989.
So far it has had little impact on daily life but businesses fear the shutdown in freight service will start to bite into earnings if the strike lasts longer.
Cities have added buses to relieve commmuter pressure, but international trains have been stranded at borders with Germany, Poland, Austria, and Slovakia.
